critical_path.title: Pagination - Navigate to the Last Page and Verify Data Integrity
critical_path.description: This test verifies the pagination functionality by navigating to the last page of quotes and ensuring that the displayed quotes and author information are correct and that there are no unexpected errors.

steps.action: Navigate to the quotes page.
steps.expected: The quotes page loads successfully, displaying the first page of quotes.

steps.action: Click the 'Last Page' button.
steps.expected: The application navigates to the last page of quotes.

steps.action: Verify the displayed quotes and author information.
steps.expected: All quotes on the last page are displayed correctly with accurate author information.

assertions: The application successfully navigates to the last page.
The correct quotes are displayed on the last page.
Author information for each quote on the last page is accurate.
No errors are displayed during the navigation or data loading process.

critical_path.title: Tag Filtering - Verify Quotes are Filtered Correctly Based on Tag Selection
critical_path.description: This test verifies that selecting a tag filters the displayed quotes correctly, showing only quotes associated with that tag.  It confirms data integrity by validating displayed quotes and author details.

steps.action: Navigate to the quotes page.
steps.expected: The quotes page loads successfully, displaying the default set of quotes.

steps.action: Click on a specific tag link (e.g., 'Inspirational').
steps.expected: The application filters the quotes, displaying only those associated with the 'Inspirational' tag.

steps.action: Verify the displayed quotes and author information.
steps.expected: All quotes displayed are tagged with 'Inspirational', and the author information is accurate for each quote.

assertions: Only quotes associated with the selected tag are displayed.
The author information for each displayed quote is accurate.
The selected tag is visually highlighted or indicated as active.
No unexpected errors are displayed during the filtering process.

validation.title: Pagination: Check boundary conditions and data consistency across pages
validation.description: Verify that the pagination controls function correctly at the boundaries (first and last page), and that data remains consistent across all pages.  Focuses on avoiding missing or duplicate data.

steps.action: Navigate to the first page of quotes.
steps.expected: First page of quotes is displayed with correct number of items per page.

steps.action: Navigate to the last page of quotes.
steps.expected: Last page of quotes is displayed with correct number of items and pagination shows no 'next' page.

steps.action: Navigate back to the first page. Verify the first quote displayed is the same.
steps.expected: The first quote matches the first quote viewed originally.

steps.action: Click 'Next' page repeatedly until the last page.
steps.expected: Each page loads correctly with a consistent number of items per page except possibly the last page, and the pagination controls update accordingly.

steps.action: Click 'Previous' page repeatedly until the first page.
steps.expected: Each page loads correctly with a consistent number of items per page, and the pagination controls update accordingly.

assertions: The first page is accessible and displays the expected number of quotes.
The last page is accessible and displays the expected number of quotes (or a smaller number if the total number of quotes is not a multiple of the page size).
No errors occur during navigation between pages.
Data remains consistent across different page visits; the same quote appears only once in the entire set of pages.

validation.title: Tag Filtering: Test with a variety of tags, including potentially malicious input.
validation.description: Validate the tag filtering functionality, ensuring correct filtering and preventing XSS vulnerabilities via tag names in URLs.

steps.action: Select a tag from the list of available tags (e.g., 'Inspirational').
steps.expected: Only quotes associated with the selected tag are displayed.

steps.action: Clear the tag filter.
steps.expected: All quotes are displayed.

steps.action: Attempt to manually modify the tag URL parameter to include XSS payload (e.g., `<script>alert('XSS')</script>`).
steps.expected: The application either sanitizes the input, encodes the characters, or rejects the input to prevent the script from executing.

steps.action: Attempt to manually modify the tag URL parameter to include SQL injection attempt (e.g., `'; DROP TABLE quotes; --`).
steps.expected: The application either sanitizes the input or rejects it, preventing SQL injection.

assertions: Quotes displayed after selecting a tag are correctly filtered based on that tag.
Clearing the tag filter returns all quotes.
The application is resistant to XSS vulnerabilities through tag URL parameters.
The application is resistant to SQL injection attacks through tag URL parameters.

error_handling.title: Pagination with Invalid Page Number
error_handling.description: Tests the system's response when an invalid page number (out of range or non-numeric) is provided in the pagination URL.  This aims to verify that the system handles unexpected input gracefully and prevents potential server errors.

steps.action: User manually navigates to a pagination URL with a negative page number (e.g., `?page=-1`)
steps.expected: System redirects to the first page (page 1) or displays a user-friendly error message indicating the invalid page number.

steps.action: User manually navigates to a pagination URL with a page number exceeding the total number of pages (e.g., `?page=9999`, if only 10 pages exist)
steps.expected: System redirects to the last page or displays a user-friendly error message indicating the invalid page number.

steps.action: User manually navigates to a pagination URL with a non-numeric page number (e.g., `?page=abc`)
steps.expected: System redirects to the first page (page 1) or displays a user-friendly error message indicating the invalid page number.

assertions: Application handles invalid page numbers gracefully without crashing or displaying server errors.
User is redirected to a valid page or shown an appropriate error message.
Data integrity is maintained - no incorrect or missing data is displayed as a result of the invalid pagination request.

error_handling.title: Tag Filtering with Malicious Input (XSS)
error_handling.description: Tests for potential XSS vulnerabilities when filtering by tags.  This test attempts to inject malicious JavaScript code through a tag URL to verify that the system properly sanitizes input and prevents execution of arbitrary code in the user's browser.

steps.action: User manually navigates to a tag filter URL containing malicious JavaScript code (e.g., `?tag=<script>alert('XSS')</script>`)
steps.expected: The injected JavaScript code is not executed. The page loads without displaying the alert, and the quotes are filtered appropriately (or an error message is shown if the tag doesn't exist).

steps.action: Inspect the HTML source code of the page after the above action.
steps.expected: The injected JavaScript code is properly escaped or removed in the HTML source code, preventing its execution by the browser.

assertions: Injected JavaScript code is not executed, preventing XSS attacks.
Input is properly sanitized or encoded before being rendered in the HTML.
The system is protected against malicious code injection through tag URLs.
